**Service key:** `ctx.skills` — class `SkillRegistry` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill`, bound via `super(ctx, 'skills')` (`packages/skill/skill/src/index.ts:374`). Only **five public methods** exist:

```ts
registerProvider(create: (control: SkillProviderControl) => SkillProvider): () => void  // :390
register(skill: SkillRegistration): () => void                                          // :439
async list(options: SkillViewOptions = {}): Promise<SkillSummary[]>                     // :470
async snapshot(options: SkillViewOptions = {}): Promise<SkillCatalogSnapshot>           // :481
async get(name: string, options: SkillViewOptions = {}): Promise<SkillDefinition | undefined>  // :500
```

No `unregister`/`remove`/`has`/`invalidate` on the service.

**Provider seam: yes, first-class.** `SkillProvider { readonly name; readonly list(options) => Promise<readonly SkillCandidate[] | SkillProviderObservation>; readonly get(candidate, options) => Promise<SkillDefinition|undefined> }` (`:247-267`); an array return is complete-discovery shorthand, `{candidates, complete:false}` is degraded-and-uncacheable. Factory gets `SkillProviderControl { signal, invalidate() }` (`:270-275`). Composition is layered: nearest scope layer wins a name outright, then within a layer `rank → providerOrder → localOrder` (project-dsh 100 … user-agents 500, runtime 250, bundled 600).

**Dependency declaration:** `export const inject = ['skills']`. The `declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' { interface Context { skills: SkillRegistry } }` augmentation is *published by the skill package itself* (`:283-298`) — an author only needs `import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill'`.

**Most important gotcha — the scoping asymmetry:** *writes infer scope from the calling context; reads require it explicitly.* `ctx.skills.register(...)` through a plain plugin context → global layer (all agents). Through `agentCtx` in `setup(agentCtx, agent)` → that agent's layer only. But `list/snapshot/get` **never infer**: omitting `options.scope` reads the global layer alone, so an agent-scoped skill is invisible unless you pass `scope: agent` (as the real `skill` tool does at `tool-skill/src/index.ts:133`).

Secondary: `candidate.provider` must equal `provider.name` or validation throws; `'runtime'` is reserved; same-name `register()` in one layer is first-wins-with-warning and returns a **no-op disposer**. Noted explicitly: no production in-repo caller of `register()` — all shipped skills are providers.

## Direct answers

**Did I find the source? Yes.** `https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya`, pinned at **`c73908d96ff73c0062c340a11bf7c54ec7d8bc4d`** (tag `v0.4.6`), **Apache-2.0**. The npm name `laya-ts` really does 404 — the source does not.

**Did it build? Yes — observed, exit 0.** `npm ci` (115 packages, 0 vulns) → `npm run build` → 26 files in `dist/`. `npm test` → **886 tests, 0 failed**. `npm run test:package` → 1/1, packing and installing into an external ESM TypeScript consumer. **There is no build blocker.**

**Did the export run? Yes, but only after a genuine defect was found and diagnosed.**

```
UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '\u2705'
```

`torch.onnx` prints a ✅ progress glyph; this console is **code page 437**, Python's stdout maps to `cp1252`, and the export aborts *inside a `print()`* before writing anything. Re-running the **same command with only `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`** → exit 0, artifacts written. **`--no-verify` was never used.**

**The specific blocker** is exactly that — a Windows console-encoding gap in the documented command. Not a source, build, export or numerics defect, and **not a registry 404**. Two facts a packaging plan must absorb: the export is **1.29 GB across six files** (external `.data` tensors — shipping only the two `.onnx` files won't load), and the tokenizer/config are SHA256-identical to the checkpoint.

**Parity — five independent checks, all green, none weakened:** export verify 3/3 (worst `1.0e-06`); cross-runtime PyTorch-vs-ONNX-in-Node `errors: 0`; 194 weight-free upstream ONNX checks; CI gate `test_onnx.py` 2 passed.

## The finding that matters most

The ONNX gate made **the library itself** warn, unprompted, that it clamps a shipped temperature `0.10058280825614929 → 0.5` and that the resulting confidence is **uncalibrated** — and I verified the **TypeScript** runtime does the same (`agent.ts:435,455-456`). So `confidence` here is a value its own runtime has already disclaimed, surfaced only as a stderr line.

**Quality is untouched by runtime availability: DEC-08 is still `NOT_RUN`, and this work does not advance it.** Multilingual sits at 0.342 accuracy against a 0.461 majority-class baseline. Packaging does not make it a reliable default.

## Two things I deliberately did not do

I did **not** run `verify/numerics_check.py` (needs ~2.2 GB more checkpoints — so the RoPE-base and SDPA-vs-eager assertions remain uncovered), and I did **not** create `packages/extension-laya/`. Step 5 is permitted since the build genuinely succeeded, but packaging turns on decisions I don't own — caching 1.29 GB through `asset-acquisition.ts`, **Licensing placement**, and how a not-yet-DEC-08 model is presented. One concrete blocker for whoever builds it: the operator store places packages where they have **no `node_modules`**, so a Laya extension importing `onnxruntime-node` will hit `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` unless that gap is solved first.

I created only the one findings file; `packages/extension-laya/` does not exist, and everything else in `git status` is the parent's concurrent work.
